Region: Southern Canaan and the Negev, associated with Caleb's family
History: The Kenizzites are named in the land promise of Genesis 15:19 and nowhere else as a nation. Their fame comes through one man: Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite (Numbers 32:12; Joshua 14:6), who followed the LORD fully and received Hebron as his inheritance. Though called a Kenizzite, Caleb was counted with the tribe of Judah. Kenaz, named in 1 Chronicles 4:13-15, belongs to the same family line, and Othniel son of Kenaz took Debir and became a judge.
Culture: Little is recorded beyond their place in the Genesis 15 list and Caleb's line. They appear as a southern clan absorbed into Judah rather than as a separate kingdom.
Religion: No distinct Kenizzite religion is described. Caleb's faithfulness is the family's mark in the text.
BibleConnection: Through Caleb the Kenizzite, this obscure people of the promise list produced one of Israel's great heroes of faith, the spy who believed God could give the land.
